details:
Honestly, I support the introduction of something that actually prevents client modifications in a serious way. There is only one thing about the blog post that didn't sit well with me:
One of the main focuses of the blog post is on individual user safety, and how  dangerous it could be to install mods. This is a very understandable concern, and I appreciate that you actually posted numbers ("thousands every month") to back things up and prove how serious of a problem it is.
However, it seems like OSC was implemented to help ease the transition away from modded clients, but **OSC is even more dangerous than client mods for the average user**, namely because you have to download and run completely separate external programs. Because of this, it's a lot harder to make a standardized "modloader" equivalent for OSC (especially because every avatar will use different OSC options), which makes community-driven security much harder.
I think the only real options to fix this are to either increase the power of avatars so that people won't need to use OSC at all for things that previously needed mods (via something like a lighter Udon system), OR to somehow make an OSC listener built into the vrchat client that has 1. a place to put user-created scripts to manage them more securely and 2. hooks back into the game that allow OSC messages to influence the game.
The main thing that I had in mind when writing this post was for a "grabbable avatars" system, which I know already has decent implementations in Udon, but most worlds don't have it. Also, having it run client-side has real benefits, both in terms of ease of use and in terms of not affecting others' performance (although I don't know how significant the performance drop is in this case, I could imagine situations where it could be much larger).
title: OSC security concerns re: EAC
